title: Microsoft Purview DLP: matched sender, recipient, subject and attachment conditions in Exchange Online alerts
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documents the matched-condition details, licensing, permissions and audit controls, and the roadmap facts match. The checklist's instruction to tune DLP rules has no corresponding control row; remove that instruction to keep the checklist aligned with the table.

claims.claim: This is a Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention change.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention - Enriched Audit Data for Matched Rules

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Exchange Online DLP alerts show every non-SIT condition that contributed to the policy match.
claims.quote: When an Exchange Online DLP policy matches a message, the DLP alert and the corresponding Activity Explorer event surface enhanced detail for every non-sensitive information type (SIT) condition that contributed to the match.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Activity Explorer shows enhanced non-SIT matched-condition details for Exchange Online DLP events.
claims.quote: For Exchange Online DLP events, Activity Explorer surfaces enhanced matched condition details for non-sensitive information type (SIT) conditions in addition to SIT matches.

claims.claim: The enhanced details are additional to SIT matches.
claims.quote: For Exchange Online DLP events, Activity Explorer surfaces enhanced matched condition details for non-sensitive information type (SIT) conditions in addition to SIT matches.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Each matched condition displays its condition name.
claims.quote: Condition name: The specific policy condition that was matched, for example, Sender domain is or Attachment's file extension is.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Each matched condition displays the actual matched value, such as contoso.com or .docx.
claims.quote: Matched value: The actual value that triggered the condition match, for example, contoso.com or .docx.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Each matched condition displays the source part of the message, such as header, envelope or attachment.
claims.quote: Source: The part of the message where the match was found, for example, the message header, envelope, or attachment.

claims.claim: The supported categories are sender, recipient, attachment, content, header and message property conditions.
claims.quote: The following condition categories are supported: Sender conditions; Recipient conditions; Attachment conditions; Content conditions; Header conditions; Message property conditions

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure

claims.where: title; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Subject contains words is a supported non-SIT matched condition.
claims.quote: Message property conditions: Message size over, Message type is, Message importance is, Subject contains words, Subject matches patterns, Subject or body contains words

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk

claims.quote: Microsoft Purview supports showing matched conditions in a DLP event to reveal the exact cause for a flagged DLP policy. This information shows up in: DLP Alerts console; Activity explorer. In the Events tab, open Details to see Other matched conditions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning auditing off makes Purview audit searches and Search-UnifiedAuditLog return no results.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results. Running the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; controls[1].governs; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Activity Explorer's activity information comes from the Microsoft 365 unified audit log.
claims.quote: The activity information comes from the Microsoft 365 unified audit logs. It's transformed and then made available in the activity explorer UI.

claims.claim: Activity Explorer is not real time.
claims.quote: Activity explorer isn't a real-time view. Because its data comes from the Microsoft 365 unified audit log, activities appear on the same schedule as audit records — not the moment they occur.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises allowing 60 to 90 minutes for Exchange activity to appear in Activity Explorer.
claims.quote: For core services (Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams), allow 60 to 90 minutes after an activity for it to appear in activity explorer. Other services can take longer, and Microsoft doesn't guarantee a specific time for an activity to become available.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity enables audit recording.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. If the Audit solution card isn't displayed, select View all solutions and then select Audit from the Core section. Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns on unified audit logging.
claims.quote: Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: The audit-enabling command must be run in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Complete the following steps to turn on auditing by using Exchange Online PowerShell: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Audit logging is generally on by default for Microsoft 365 organisations, subject to the stated SMB and unmanaged-trial exceptions.
claims.quote: Audit logging is on by default for Microsoft 365 organizations.

claims.claim: SMB licences including Business Premium do not have auditing enabled by default and require manual enablement.
claims.quote: Auditing isn't enabled by default for Small and Medium Business (SMB) licenses, including Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Business Standard, and Business Premium. In both these cases, you must manually enable auditing for your organization.

claims.claim: Unmanaged tenants using free trials of enterprise licences do not have auditing enabled by default and require manual enablement.
claims.quote: Additionally, unmanaged tenants that use free trials of enterprise licenses don't have auditing enabled by default. In both these cases, you must manually enable auditing for your organization.

claims.claim: The Compliance Management and Organization Management role groups hold the Exchange Online Audit Logs role by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Compliance Management and Organization Management role groups on the Permissions page in the Exchange admin center have this role.

claims.claim: Audit > Search in the Microsoft Purview portal is the route to audit search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select the Audit solution card. On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog searches the unified audit log.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. That means you can use this cmdlet to search the audit log instead of using the search tool on the Audit page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Audit search requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log. To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: The audit search operation reads records rather than changing enhanced matched-condition behaviour.
claims.quote: Search in Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium) gives your organization access to critical audit log event data so you can gain insight and further investigate user activities.

claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to tune DLP rules is covered by the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: Use the matched values to tune rules that fire on common sender domains or attachment extensions. Table: Whether the unified audit log ... records activity; Searching the audit records that feed Activity Explorer.
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout bullet beginning 'Use the matched values to tune rules': DLP rule configuration has no row in the controls table. Do not add a control row as part of this correction.
